summaries.demographer: Thomas Gatlin is a 9-year-old white, non-Hispanic male born August 14, 2016 in Greenville, TX, who has lived his entire life in Royse City, TX 75189 (Q85–Q89). He resides in a two-parent owner-occupied home with mother Sarah (Bachelor's-prepared registered nurse working at a family-medicine clinic in Rockwall), father Mike (self-employed residential contractor with sub-baccalaureate education), and younger sister Ellie (age 5), plus a dog (Q05, Q11, Q58, Q100–Q107). The household is intact, English-speaking, evangelical Protestant (Baptist), and economically stable enough to own their home, fund a college 529, and finance extracurriculars including piano lessons, soccer league fees, and summer art camp (Q47, Q62, Q83). He is enrolled in 4th grade at Royse City Elementary and is firmly embedded in small-town North Texas civic and religious institutions: school, First Baptist Church, youth soccer league, and regional events like the State Fair (Q21, Q47, Q91).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Thomas displays unusually deliberate consumer-saving behavior for his age: he is forgoing immediate gratification to accumulate $80 for a specific LEGO Bionicle set in a transparent mason-jar commitment device, has reached $47 after five months, and his mother has structured a savings 'match' incentive tied to his upcoming birthday (Q16, Q61). His allowance is a conditional, performance-based contract — $5/week contingent on completing all chores, with documented dock for missed recycling — and he responds to the incentive structure rationally (sticky-note reminders, occasional $4 weeks accepted as a 'slower path' to the goal) (Q16, Q81). Choice-architecture is heavily mediated by his mother (decision-elicitation via Socratic questioning) rather than imposed, which has produced a pattern of mom-anchored deliberation under uncertainty (Q03, Q05). He exhibits loss-aversion behavior in his self-described 'worrier' identity and uses sketching as a substitution good for emotional regulation rather than seeking external rewards (Q43, Q45).
summaries.political_scientist: Thomas is pre-political: he can't yet vote, refuses to identify with a party, and explicitly places himself 'in the middle' when pressed (Q23, Q95, Q96). However, his political socialization environment is heterogeneous and visible to him — father consumes Fox News, mother consumes NPR — and he has internalized this as a household tradition of mediated, non-confrontational exposure rather than partisan alignment (Q24). His civic identity is mediated overwhelmingly through institutional participation rather than ideology: church attendance, school mock elections, polling-place tag-alongs with his mother, and regional traditions like the State Fair (Q21, Q23, Q47). On race, he absorbs a values-frame ('be kind, treat everyone fair') anchored by his mother's correction of an older relative's commentary and by school-based exposure to figures like Ruby Bridges, suggesting an emergent affective egalitarianism without ideological framing (Q26–Q30).
summaries.psychologist: Thomas presents as a temperamentally cautious, internally directed child with an artist's interior life: he is described by his mother and self-describes as a 'worrier,' has been seen by a school counselor for test anxiety, and has internalized a box-breathing technique as a portable coping skill (Q43, Q45). His emotion-regulation strategies are mature for his age — sketching as affect-regulation, physical proximity to his dog Biscuit during distress, and verbal disclosure to his mother — and he showed appropriate grief and rumination during his grandfather's cardiac hospitalization, including a memorable concurrent stress-stack with a science fair deadline that his father defused through co-regulation (Q43–Q45). His identity is consolidated around three pillars: artist (primary, central, and aspirational), family-member (most-valued anchor), and learner (school as 'job') — with a clear coherent narrative voice for a 9-year-old (Q01, Q108, Q109). Cognitively he is verbally fluent, spatially capable (LEGO, Scratch), and shows early metacognitive awareness ('mom says it's complicated, which usually means I'll understand when I'm older'), but he also displays expected developmental opacity around adult-domain topics like finances, taxes, and partisan politics (Q26, Q57, Q75, Q95).
